glosses: A person or animal that steps, especially energetically or high.

examples.text: I marvel that these steppers upon flowers childishly make no provision for the pitfalls concealed beneath them.
Although Martha Haskins never won a prize at a dance, she was proud of having been “a purty good stepper."
A Motion Picture Classic writer who witnessed the Reids at the Sunset Inn wrote, “Wally is some stepper. Let me tell you the boy can dance."
Should there be a fey fiddler secreted among the musicians, or a seelie stepper on the dance floor, then the final tune of the evening could end with you dancing off with them, never to return.
Shall I call your vader then? He's a most accomplished stepper. He can show you how to dance.
He was a fancy stepper, and no doubt he figured that a good jig dance would improve his chances with Sis Hartnett.

glosses: A dancer in a step show.

examples.text: Before he entered high school, he was a "stepper,” a practitioner of a local Philadelphia dance form derived from tapping.
Just as the early circular routines of fraternity and sorority steppers suggest the influence of patting juba, so too may they reflect another early African American dance form, the “ring shout.”

Although research on this subject is somewhat inconclusive, there are several instances in which the African origins of the canes used by steppers, dancers, and Brazilian practitioners of the martial art form Maculele (which is also a dance) are documented.

glosses: A kind of electric motor that advances in steps rather than smoothly.
A device used in the manufacture of microcircuits to apply a photolithographic image repeatedly, at regular intervals (by imaging, moving a step and repeating).

examples.text: I am working out on the stepper, but I feel like dancing instead.

glosses: Anything that moves or advances in steps.

examples.text: The Age field is a numeric stepper tool that allows you to scroll through a specific range of numbers.

glosses: A shoe, especially a fashionable or attractive shoe, or one used for step-dancing.

examples.text: "And I would dress smack daddy down." Tawanda throws her head back, laughing. "The other girls was all lacy-like, with high heels; I had steppers, low heels like men's spectator shoes, and pointy toes. I got the foot for it and I got the height; I would put on the suit, the pantsuit, go out there with my megaphone, and step—I would STEP!" She hops to her feet and does a step or two.

“[…] what are you wearing tonight?” “Well, I went to the mall and found the most amazing boots ever!” “Oh God, you and these boots. Ariel, you could open up a shoe store as many shoes as you have.” “Shut up and look at my new steppers.”

On the treadmill we were shut up in little boxes, almost pitch dark, and the handrail to catch hold of when treading the mill was so high […] I refused point blank, one morning, to go on the stepper on plea of illness, […]

glosses: The feet of anthropomorphic animals, especially paws.
Trotter à vive allure en projetant nettement vers l’avant les membres antérieurs.

examples.text: Ses actions sont énergiques, brillantes, il relève à la hauteur du nez ; il steppe avec grâce, en cadence, la détente du jarret est formidable ; […] ; il y a des bonds et des hennissements ; en un mot, l’animal est splendide…

glosses: Stepper comme un cheval, pour un humain.

examples.text: – C’en est… écoute-moi, Privat… Ils en sont… Oui, les gens qui défilent là, dans la rue, et qui lancent leurs jambes en marchant comme cela – Duchenne faisait le geste de stepper –, je les ai reconnus. Ce sont des ataxiques. Ils m’appartiennent. Je vais les interroger tous, tous, tous.
